title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: production service-side continuous batching was susceptible to starvation of long-running low-throughput routes and head-of-line blocking for high-priority short requests during load spikes. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler with a combination of queueing knobs, timeout-based promotion/eviction, and aging-based fairness to prevent starvation while preserving throughput. Changes include: 1) introduce per-priority sub-queues and a configurable max_queue_ms that caps how long a request can be queued before being forced into the next dispatch window, 2) implement an aging score that gradually increases priority for requests that have waited > starvation_threshold_ms, 3) add soft-deadline eviction for oversized batches to respect latency SLOs, 4) sampling-based admission control to avoid large low-util batches delaying high-priority requests, and 5) metrics/tracing and integration tests to validate fairness and throughput impact. Configuration: new runtime flags continuous_batcher.max_queue_ms, continuous_batcher.starvation_threshold_ms, continuous_batcher.priority_windows_ms, continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens, and continuous_batcher.sample_admit_rate. Performance: on internal perf-canary workloads we observed 4-7% p95 token latency reduction for mixed-priority traces and reduced observed starvation (requests exceeding starvation_threshold_ms) from ~3.7% to <0.2% under bursty traffic. Rollout: feature gated behind continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 and default-off for Dedicated regions; staged canary rollout to 10% of serving pools before global rollout. Testing: unit tests for queueing logic, integration canary with synthetic mixed-priority workload, and end-to-end smoke tests for KV cache interaction. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current behavior unless scheduler_v2 flag enabled. See release_notes for operator guidance.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice work. A couple of questions: how does the aging score interact with KV cache locality? If we promote a long-waiting request into a batch, will we regress cache hit rate?

Asha Menon: Good point. We added a small affinity bonus in the aging score so promoted requests prefer batches with matching model shard/kv key prefixes when available, and added a unit test to assert no statistically significant drop in KV hit-rate on the canary.
Priya Patel: Can we get an optional strict-mode where starvation prevention is disabled for latency-critical tiers? We want per-tenant control.
Asha Menon: Added continuous_batcher.priority_windows_ms and an allowlist that can be set per-tenant. Default preserves current low-latency behavior for critical tiers.

merge_details: Merged via squash on 2025-02-18 by Asha Menon. Commit message: "scheduler: tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (continuous-batcher scheduler_v2)"
release_notes: Runtime: continuous-batcher scheduler v2 (opt-in). Adds per-priority sub-queues, starvation prevention via aging and timeouts, sampling-based admission control, and new runtime flags for operators. Expected benefits: improved p95 tail latency under mixed workloads and near-elimination of starvation cases. Ops: staged rollout recommended; monitor metrics continuous_batcher.queue_wait_ms, continuous_batcher.starved_requests, and kv_cache.hit_rate. Default behavior unchanged until scheduler_v2 enabled.
perf_summary: Canary workload (mixed-priority, 1k qps burst): p95 token latency reduced by 4-7%
Starvation metric (requests > starvation_threshold_ms): reduced from ~3.7% to <0.2%
Throughput: end-to-end throughput stable (+/-1%) across canary pools
KV cache hit rate: no statistically significant regression observed in canary (within 0.5% confidence interval)
notes_for_oncall: If enabling scheduler_v2, watch continuous_batcher.starved_requests and continuous_batcher.queue_wait_ms; if starved_requests spikes, reduce continuous_batcher.max_queue_ms or increase sample_admit_rate.
If KV cache hit_rate drops by >2% during rollout, consider toggling affinity bonus off and re-evaluating promoted-batch heuristics.
Rollback: disable continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 flag and restart batch workers; this reverts to previous queueing behavior without requiring model restarts.
